The go/no-go checklist verifies that all application areas and the technical team are ready for live transactions to be executed using the new or enhanced capabilities, processes and tools.

The go/no-go checklist validates a comprehensive and correctly-sequenced list of tasks, milestones, and critical events to support cut-over related go/no-go decisions. It is meant to be a single source of tasks to be performed by all teams during a cutover. It helps to define detailed business area-specific and team-specific cutover plans.

Design the checklist to review preparation activities and tasks that are on the critical path to executing the cutover. Critical path areas that the checklist helps confirm readiness for include:

  • Production code and configuration
  • Data migration
  • Production infrastructure
  • Operations support and monitoring
  • Service management process and procedure
  • Roles and access
  • End user
  • Training

More generally, when compiling the checklist, consider including confirmation of:

  • Conversions verified
  • Manual conversions identified and tested
  • Legacy system plans executed
  • Integration testing complete
  • Final system test accepted
  • Test environment for mock or dress rehearsal set up
  • Testing of access, user and customers complete
  • Command center set up
  • Procedures documentation complete and distributed
  • Communications established
  • End user training complete
  • Final sign-off complete
  • Initial authority to operate granted

After the go/no-go checklist is drafted, it is important to bring all stakeholders and program leadership together to gain agreement from stakeholders that the checklist is reasonable and complete, that the checklist does not leave out any critical items that must be addressed prior to go-live.

Transition managers should arrange necessary meetings, seek input from all impacted parties, and finalize the checklist items. Stakeholders whose input should be considered include:

  • Business leads from all functional areas
  • Technical project leads
  • Data migration leads
  • Change management leads
  • Overall project lead

Stakeholders should seek input on the checklist from members of their teams who have been assigned to execute tasks on the checklist.

Once the go/no-go checklist has been agreed by stakeholders, leaders should communicate results to the organization.

A thorough cutover checklist will encompass activities from all phases of the project, beginning with planning.  It will include pre-cutover tasks, will consider production system builds, system cutover activities, third-party system cutover activities, batch job scheduling and interface scheduling and activation.

Communications are an important aspect of cutover.  The checklist should be a part of planning materials which also include:

  • Go/no go meeting and communication of the result
  • Go-live planning activities
  • Business continuity plans
  • Hypercare team resources and plan
  • Post go-live resource plan
  • Post go-live training requirements
To document the information that will verify the organization's readiness to proceed with the cutover.

Confirm production code and configuration readiness

Confirm that all configurations required are in place prior to cutover and also to confirm the development code is ready for migration to production. Confirm that all the teams have followed and implemented the configuration steps required and executed the necessary test scripts to validate the configuration and freeze configuration activities.

  • Validate that all development activities are complete per functional and technical specifications developed as part of detailed design.
  • Validate that all configuration steps have been completed as per functional specifications.
  • Validate the execution of unit tests and functional test scripts.
  • Evaluate the status of critical defect resolution from test script execution.
  • Review the results from those steps to confirm if the development code and configuration are ready to move to production and communicate readiness to the project team.
  • After reviewing results, if there are significant concerns about code and configuration readiness move to production, then communicate the situation (with plan for resolution) to the project team.

Prior to code migration to production, all teams must complete development activities, testing, bug fixes and code freeze. Teams must also confirm that all unit testing, functional testing and user acceptance testing is completed, and the code is ready for migration to production.

Confirm readiness of data to be migrated, along with associated programs, applications, processes, and team prior to performing data migration. Raise awareness of potential data migration issues, mitigate data quality risks, and verify timely completion of data migration activities within the available window. This can have significant downstream impact to future go-live and operational activities.

  • Organize a meeting to include data migration coordinator, basis lead, and other team leads.
  • In the meeting, using the data migration readiness checklist, confirm whether the data migration activities can be started.
  • Once readiness is signed off for data migration, communicate the news to project team and project steering committee members.

Element.attribute:
Confirm with the infrastructure team whether the completely configured technical production environment is ready to support productive operations.

Upon completion of this task, cutover activities such as production code migration, configuration migration to production, and data migration can begin. This step also confirms the production system readiness for other production activities.

Call a meeting with infrastructure team leads to review the infrastructure readiness report. Using the report:

  • Confirm that all the required hardware is in place
  • Confirm all the necessary software is installed
  • Confirm external systems are configured to production system
  • Review infrastructure test results to validate all issues during tests have been addressed
  • User access and authorizations are set up

Once the infrastructure readiness report is reviewed and it's confirmed that the system is ready for production activities, communicate readiness to the project team.

Element.attribute: Confirm operations support and monitoring readiness
Confirm operations support and monitoring readiness

Confirm that the help desk and other first-level support are in place and prepared to monitor systems operations and are prepared to address or triage issues as they are raised. Verify that the initial support structure is prepared for the go-live. 

  • Validate Level 1 support personnel readiness (training complete, on-site as required, etc.): tool readiness (software installed, tested, users trained on use, etc.); and staffing schedule (check for adequate main shift and (if required) off-shift coverage is prepared and available). Approve operations support structure by site.
  • Validate Level 1 support personnel readiness (training complete, on-site as required, etc.).
  • Validate Level 1 tool readiness (software installed, tested, users trained on use, etc.).
  • Validate staffing schedule (check that adequate main shift and (if required) off-shift coverage is prepared and available).
  • Approve operations support structure by site.  

Excellent Level 1 service is required so that minor issues, questions, and defects are addressed quickly and efficiently. Without properly structured Level 1 support, too many minor issues will have to be elevated to Level 2, 3, or 4 support, which will both delay resolution of these issues as well as reduce the ability of high-level support to work on more critical and complex issues.

Operations support can either be on or off-site, depending on the requirements of the individual site. In addition, proper staffing and scheduling must be determined so that high-demand periods have proper coverage (either remote help or in-person), and coverage is also present during off-shifts as determined by project management.

Element.attribute: Confirm service management process and procedure readiness
Confirm service management process and procedure readiness

Verify that all service management processes and procedures are complete and ready for cutover. Verify that the service management team is ready for cutover and that all necessary service management procedures are in place.

  • Confirm knowledge transfer has happened successfully to the service management team (Levels 1 and 2)
  • Approve and accept documentation of operations, including operational and support policy, roles, processes, procedures and metrics
  • Define and agree upon operational level agreements
  • Define and agree upon full RACI between support and business system administrators
  • Verify that functional and hierarchical escalation paths are documented and agreed upon across operations, business, and service providers

A checklist is typically used by the project manager and service management lead to verify that each item is complete and has been verified by the appropriate owner. The checklist should typically include:

  • Training sign-off - business leads and trainers should verify that all requested or required is complete or will be complete by go-live
  • Roles are ready for migration to production
  • Production support issue resolution procedures are in place and properly staffed
  • Confirmation that all service management policies, procedures and reporting are ready

This is one of the steps within the process to agree the overall go/no-go decision.

Element.attribute:
Verify that all roles-related activities are complete and ready for cutover. Confirm that roles are ready for cutover and that all necessary maintenance procedures are in place.

  • Review completed list of end-users
  • Validate all provisioning tasks in the project plan have been completed
  • Select a random sample of user IDs for review in production system
  • Validate correct user provisioning in the production system based on a sample
  • Confirm user provisioning is complete in the production system

A checklist should be prepared, checked and verified to confirm that all production-related roles activities are in place and ready for cutover. The checklist is typically used by the project manager to confirm that each item is complete and has been verified by the appropriate owner. These include:

  • Training signoff by business leads and trainers, to verify that all requested or required training is complete or will be complete by go-live
  • Conduct business readiness testing of all roles to verify that everyone can access the system with the appropriate system access capabilities
  • Resolve any outstanding issues; verify that the role owner matrix is complete and that all required access has been granted and verified
  • Confirm operations support monitoring readiness by confirming that the ability to resolve roles issues is in place and that monitoring and reporting is addressed

This is one of the steps within the agree go/no-go cutover decision process.

Element.Name: Confirm end user readiness
Element.copyright:
© 2012, 2022 EYGM Limited. All Rights Reserved.
Privacy Notice

Powered by Global Methods in conjunction with Consulting Methods
Element.attribute:
Confirm that end-users are fully ready to operate the integrated solution. Verify that the end users (personnel who will be using the solution in an operational and day-to-day capacity) are prepared to make the go-live a success.

This confirmation also a chance for the solution deployment team to confirm that organizational change management of the end users has progressed sufficiently to enable go-live success, and also prepare for the go-live stabilization phase of the deployment. It validates the effectiveness of the training delivered, the effectiveness of the communication plan, and the overall buy-in from personnel at all operational levels to the solution. It can also provide the deployment team with forewarning of any areas of the solution that the end users are not fully prepared for, which will then allow the deployment team to brief the front-line support on items of concern.

  • Review current go-live checklist
  • Confirm training attendance and completion
  • Confirm end-user communications published and received
  • Confirm standard operating procedures (SOP) and job aids are updated and distributed
  • Confirm key dates and activities have been communicated
  • Confirm end-user provisioning has been completed and unlock process is in place
  • Obtain formal end-user readiness assessment from team leads and stakeholders
  • Confirm end-user readiness in project plans and checklists 

A checklist should be used to confirm that all areas are accounted for and planned prior to kick-off. The appropriate personnel should also be involved in the final decision when considering whether this confirmation is final. Techniques employed to determine readiness may include:

  • Selection of criteria
  • Survey composed and distributed
  • End users interviewed
  • Quizzes and interview results evaluated
  • Job aids distributed
  • One-on-one discussions held
  • Confirmation of readiness obtained
  • Training

The readiness assessment should be informed by knowledge of the solution to be deployed, a basic understanding of the benefits, knowledge of the deployment plan for the site, and understanding of the resources available to assist the end users in the go-live process.

  • Check that all support staff training is complete
  • Check that scheduling and class participation is confirmed if additional training is required due to staggered implementations, additional locations, or other reasons
